chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Amr ibn Jumay', who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

There is no harm in performing iq'a' during prayer between the two prostrations, between the first and second rak'a, and between the third and fourth rak'a. And if the Imam makes you sit in a place where you must stand, then withdraw (from it). And iq'a' is not permissible in the place of the two testimonies (tashahhud) except due to an illness, because the one who performs iq'a' is not considered legally sitting; he has only sat with some part of his body on another part.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَيْنِ: The two testimonies (tashahhud) recited in prayer.
key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: The two prostrations in a rak'a.
key_terms.الِاقْعَاء: Iq'a: A sitting posture where one sits on the heels with the buttocks raised off the ground.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sit on the heels (iq'a) during the tashahhud in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s distinction between the permissible 'iq'a' (sitting on heels) during transitional moments of prayer and its prohibition during the formal tashahhud, where a complete seated posture is required. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical completeness of the sitting position (julus) for the testimony, contrasting it with the partial sitting allowed in other intervals, reflecting the detailed attention to prayer postures (sunnah) in Imami fiqh.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Ahmad bin Ziyad bin Ja’far al-Hamdani, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Amru bin Jumay’, that he said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:

There is no harm in performing iq’a’ during prayer between the two prostrations, between the first and second rak’a and between the third and fourth rak’a. If the leader (in prayer) makes you sit in a place in which you must stand in, then withdraw from it. It is not permissible to perform iq’a’ in the place of the (reciting of the) two testimonies, except if due to an illness, because the one who performs iq’a’ is not (legally defined as) sitting, but he would only have sat with some part of himself on another part. Iq’a’ is that a man places his buttocks on his heel bones during his (reciting of the) testification.
